title: Natural derived tensor comparison for independently localized open restriction
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U any open, and choose independently localized derived categories D(X), D(U) [def-pc-derived-category] with their fixed derived tensor structures [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. For exact derived open restriction R [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps], there is a natural isomorphism of bifunctors R(E tensor F) ≅ R(E) tensor R(F). There are no boundedness, quasi-coherence, separation or nonemptiness hypotheses.

source.place: Derived tensor construction; Tag 08EU first sentence (locality); K-flat model expansion of the tensor-restriction part.

proof.text: Identify canonical open restriction with the adjoint module pullback along the open immersion, using overFunctorEquiv and restrictFunctorIsoPullback. Transport the strong monoidal structure of pullbackMonoidal to restriction. Restriction preserves all small coproducts by the over-site construction and the over equivalence. Apply the proved source-library mapBifunctorComparisonNatTrans to obtain a natural isomorphism between restriction of the signed total tensor and the signed total tensor of restrictions.

Take the full subcategory of K-flat complexes and its inclusion F. Apply kFlat_derivedTensor_comparison_natIso to the pair F,F on X, and to the restricted pair F⋙RC,F⋙RC on U; openRestriction_isKFlat verifies the latter hypothesis. Compose the first comparison postcomposed by derived restriction, mapDerivedCategoryFactors on the total-tensor models, the natural total-tensor restriction comparison, the inverse local K-flat comparison, and the inverse tensor of mapDerivedCategoryFactors on the two inputs. The private abstract tensorModelComposition performs this composition of natural isomorphisms without unfolding concrete localization functors.

Use naturality of the assembled model isomorphism separately in each variable to obtain simultaneous naturality on K-flat pairs. Apply kFlat_bifunctor_iso_descent to the bifunctors curriedTensorPost RD and curriedTensorPre RD, with the independently localized derived category of U as the arbitrary target category. The descent theorem supplies a natural isomorphism of curried derived bifunctors. Take its component at each pair to build the required isomorphism of product-category functors; its naturality follows by factoring a tensor morphism into the two whiskerings and composing the two naturality squares. No boundedness or nonempty-open hypotheses enter.

lean.statement:
theorem derivedTensor_openRestriction_natIso (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wO} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))] :
    let R := (schemeOpenRestriction X U).mapDerivedCategory
    Nonempty (tensor (schemeDerivedCategory X) ⋙ R ≅
      R.prod R ⋙ tensor (schemeDerivedCategory U.toScheme))
